coverage_explanation: Exercises automatic tracking under maximal opposite light imbalances and a repeated reversal. Comparisons accept any distinct commanded angles without requiring a minimum angular separation. Mounting direction is unspecified, so these checks establish response to reversal rather than absolute physical orientation. Charging thresholds, low-voltage duration, voltage scaling, display contents, and manual-calibration controls are unspecified; those behaviors cannot be independently asserted reliably and remain uncovered.
assumptions: Uses the disclosed bench defaults: D2 is a button to GND with INPUT_PULLUP, released HIGH. It remains explicitly released during this automatic-tracking test.
A0, A1, and A2 use raw ADC values 0..1023 and the default 5 V reference. A2 stays constant to isolate tracking; no application charging threshold is inferred.
Servo mounting orientation, starting angle, travel limits, adjustment increments, and tracking period are unspecified. Opposite sustained imbalances are checked for distinct commanded positions only.
Each light state is held for 20 seconds as a practical finite-suite response allowance, not a requirement-defined deadline.

The reference selects illustrative unspecified parameters: 0..180 degree travel, a 20-count light deadband, one-degree steps every 20 ms, direct 5 V voltage scaling, a 3 V low-charge threshold lasting 10 seconds, and voltage display in hundredths of a volt. Checks do not mandate these choices.

The reference implements usable manual calibration by mapping the relative A0/A1 readings to a manually selectable angle while in manual mode. Each debounced button press toggles modes. This calibration interface is a permitted design choice, not a candidate test assertion.
